caption:
Arriving in Morro de São Paulo can feel confusing the first time.

Here are five things we wish every visitor knew before the trip: how the island works, why your route from Salvador matters, and where to go when you want a slower day.

Send us your arrival date and we'll help you choose the easiest way to arrive.

campos.label: Island guide
campos.title: 5 things to know before visiting *Morro de São Paulo*
campos.subtitle: A calm guide for your first time on Ilha de Tinharé
campos.alt: Natural pools at Quarta Praia, Morro de São Paulo

campos.label: It's an island
campos.title: Morro de São Paulo is on *Ilha de Tinharé*
campos.body: You arrive by sea, so the way you travel from Salvador shapes the first day of your trip.
campos.alt: Aerial view of the port and coast of Morro de São Paulo, with boats and the lighthouse

campos.label: How to arrive
campos.title: There is more than *one route*
campos.body: Regular, semi-terrestrial or private. Each one works differently depending on your flight time and your luggage.

campos.label: Beyond Morro
campos.title: The island is *bigger* than its most famous village
campos.body: Garapuá, Gamboa and Boipeba are part of the same coastline, each with its own pace.
campos.alt: Green coast of Gamboa on Ilha de Tinharé, seen from above

campos.label: From the water
campos.title: Some places are best seen *by boat*
campos.body: Boat tours reach natural pools, hidden beaches and quiet villages around the island.
campos.alt: A boat leaving a wake along the coast near Morro de São Paulo

campos.label: No rush
campos.title: Plan your arrival *before* you travel
campos.body: It's not just about arriving, but about arriving without stress.
campos.alt: The lighthouse of Morro de São Paulo at sunset

campos.title: Plan your arrival with people who *know the island*
campos.body: Ask us about transfers and day tours around Ilha de Tinharé.
